feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader: the experience is relevant, progressive, and supported by concrete scope indicators. It reads professionally, but it is slightly dense and repetitive, with some formatting/style inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior positioning: the headline, summary, and career progression at NACo strongly support leadership credibility in digital platforms, governance, analytics, and multimedia.  
- Good use of scale and scope: metrics like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers” add impact and trust.  
- Broad, relevant skill coverage: technical, strategic, editorial, and production capabilities are well aligned to public-sector digital leadership roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition and tighten structure: “digital strategy / governance / workflows / content operations” appears across summary, competencies, skills, and roles. Consolidate overlapping sections, especially Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results. Include measurable improvements in engagement, efficiency, adoption, search performance, or campaign outcomes.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “organization-wide” and “member-facing” are consistent, but punctuation/bullet formatting is uneven; “Coleman DAVIS” is stylistically inconsistent unless intentional branding. No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible positioning with clear seniority and sector focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly broad and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and experience sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten to one sharper value proposition and add 1–2 concrete signals of scale or scope from recent roles.
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct, active phrasing like “leading modernization of” or “designing and scaling.”
- Reduce the list of functions; group related areas to improve flow and avoid sounding like a skills dump.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Builds and scales digital platforms, editorial systems, and AI-enabled user experiences that improve discovery, publishing efficiency, and audience engagement across complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; keep it brief here.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” closely echoes the subtitle and skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align with the headline and recent roles, but the section is broad and overlaps heavily with Topline Skills and the header. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing leadership-level scope will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use sharper, executive-level wording and reduce filler terms like “operations” where possible.
- Reorder for strongest relevance/recency: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI/search, automation, then communications/multimedia.
- Consider this rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, dashboards and reporting infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream delivery
- Keep style consistent: use either “and” or “&” throughout; “and” reads more polished.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; consider making Core Competencies more strategic while leaving tools/platforms to later sections.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” overlaps with both Work Experience and Technical + IT.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads like a repeat of the experience section and is slightly too dense for a footer. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing outcomes or distinct scope will make it more scannable and additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use consistent action verbs and style: e.g., “Built,” “Developed,” “Launched,” “Produced.”
- Replace vague phrases like “designed for continued campaign growth” with sharper wording such as “built for ongoing campaign expansion.”
- Standardize formatting and punctuation; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for consistency and readability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and the advocacy video series closely overlap with current/future-facing bullets in Work Experience.
- Consider keeping only the most distinctive projects here, especially the anniversary campaign and conference display, which add new texture not covered elsewhere.

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Website

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good strategic/technical range, but it reads as a task list. Tighten the opening, foreground the highest-value outcomes, and avoid repeating governance/workflow themes already covered in the NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with a sharper scope statement: “Embedded as a full-time freelance consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital strategy, Drupal-based campaign experiences, and enterprise web improvement.”
- Convert bullets to impact-led phrasing: “Built organization-wide content workflows, analytics, and digital systems to improve coordination across communications teams.”
- Combine overlapping platform bullets: “Designed and launched Drupal campaign/microsite experiences, modular content components, member toolkits, and front-end/CMS enhancements for high-traffic public web properties.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: number of sites/pages supported, teams/users served, reductions in publishing time, engagement gains, search success metrics, or adoption of the AI search initiative.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, and cross-channel best practices” overlaps with NACo entries; keep only if you can show a distinct result.
- “CMS development/front-end implementation” may duplicate skills sections unless tied to a concrete business outcome.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals; it will be even stronger if you tighten the opening and add clearer outcomes from the platform, analytics, and studio work. Since this is your most senior NACo role, emphasize transformation and team/business impact over channel oversight.

Suggested edit
- Replace the opening with a sharper scope statement: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable business results where possible: email engagement growth, production cost/time savings from the studio, reporting speed/visibility improvements, or governance efficiency gains.
- Tighten weaker phrasing: change “serving thousands of followers” and “improving strategic decision-making” to specific metrics or concrete results.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the prior NACo role; keep this entry focused on leadership, modernization, and infrastructure.
- “Built NACo’s first…video studio” may echo earlier multimedia bullets; frame it here as scaling in-house production capacity and reducing external reliance.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story and relevant scope, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later NACo role and the earlier manager/producer role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing execution, channel ownership, and systems/process improvements before the director-level strategy work.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter summary: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social media and video, strengthening editorial coordination and advocacy messaging.”
- Replace “helping” language with direct ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Clarify the video impact if possible: “Launched/expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.” Add views, frequency, or audience growth if available.
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger outcome-focused line: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and cross-team coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthened editorial planning/workflows” overlaps with the Director of Digital Media entry; keep this version execution-focused, not governance-focused.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/owning the channel rather than creating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tighter, more distinctive, and skew toward senior, recent strengths shown in the 2022–present roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, senior-level wording tied to recent scope.
- Suggested rewrite:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, policy & advocacy messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- If space allows, make one line more outcome-oriented, e.g. “Enterprise digital strategy for high-traffic, multi-publisher environments.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” is very close to “Multi-channel communication” in Core Competencies and the header’s “cross-channel communications.”
- “Editorial systems and governance” overlaps with “Editorial workflow design” and “Workflow & systems architecture”; consider using “content operations” to differentiate.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill mix aligned to the recent Drupal modernization and AI-search work, but this item is too tool-list-heavy and overlaps with the separate “Technical + IT” section. It should emphasize higher-value capabilities and group tools more strategically.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint & Power Pages • CMS modernization & migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations & workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search & content discovery
- Lead with platform modernization and AI-enabled search, since those are most supported by your most recent roles.
- Replace “technical execution” style listing with capability phrasing (“Front-end implementation,” “content discovery”) to sound more senior.
- If possible, tie this section elsewhere to outcomes already in experience: 10,000+ page Drupal migration, 3.5M annual page views, enterprise search initiative.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Most tools here repeat “Technical + IT”; avoid mirroring the same list in both sections.
- “CMS modernization” also overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Web & CMS administration.”

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack for recent leadership roles, but this reads as a generic keyword list. It would be stronger if grouped around business value and framed to reflect the analytics infrastructure work highlighted in the 2022–2024 role.

Suggested edit:
- Recast from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis”
- Then add tools as supporting platforms: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity”
- Consider a tighter rewrite: “Analytics strategy & optimization: KPI design, executive dashboards, SEO/performance analysis, and reporting infrastructure across GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, and Microsoft Clarity”
- If space allows elsewhere, quantify impact in experience bullets rather than here (e.g., reporting adoption, decision-making improvements, traffic/conversion gains)

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Leadership reporting” overlaps with “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies; use “executive dashboards” or “reporting infrastructure” instead
- Tool names here may feel repetitive with the Director of Digital Media bullet; keep this section capability-first to avoid duplication

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong supporting skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with the “Multimedia & live event production” competency plus several NACo bullets. Make it more senior, specific, and aligned to recent studio-building/event leadership work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio Operations & Live Events**
- Replace with tighter, higher-value terms: **Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and multi-camera systems • In-house studio operations • Virtual event production**
- If accurate, add scale/outcome language instead of generic tasks, e.g. **Broadcast-quality studio production for advocacy programming and recurring executive content**
- Keep phrasing noun-based and parallel; avoid mixing tools, activities, and formats inconsistently

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This partially duplicates **Core Competencies: Multimedia & live event production**; consider keeping detail here and shortening/removing the broader competency mention
- “Virtual event production” and “Livestreaming” may be redundant unless you want both live broadcast and broader event-format coverage

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” This item should either be tightened to avoid repetition or reframed to emphasize platform administration/publishing environments.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Web Platforms & CMS Administration
- Replace with: Drupal (enterprise, large-scale migrations) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, prioritize strongest/recent platform first and add light context only where differentiating value exists, e.g. Drupal as primary platform.
- Keep it purely platform-focused; avoid adding modernization or technical execution language already covered elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages already appear in Topline Skills; consider removing this item entirely if both sections stay.
- GitHub Pages is the only unique entry here; if retained, this section should justify itself by adding distinct platform-administration framing.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should emphasize implementation tools not already covered elsewhere and, if possible, signal level of use or recent relevance.

Suggested edit:
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group by function to improve scanability: “Integrations & deployment: API integrations, GitHub Actions, Cloudflare Workers”
- Keep only tools you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; if GTM is light-touch, move or remove it.
- If space allows, add specificity instead of breadth, e.g. “API-driven web enhancements” or “tag management and deployment automation”

Possible rewrite:
- Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery • Integrations & deployment: API integrations, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions • Tag management: Google Tag Manager

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills may partially overlap with GitHub Actions.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with stronger, more strategic claims elsewhere. Make it more selective and frame tools by workflow value, not just names.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Systems
- Group by function to show intent and reduce list-like feel: Airtable, Power Automate, and Zapier for workflow automation and process design; Jira, Asana, and Trello for project tracking and editorial coordination; Slack and Teams for cross-team communication.
- Cut Basecamp unless it was materially used in recent roles; prioritize tools tied to current consulting/NACo work.
- If accurate, add a light impact cue in adjacent summary/experience bullets instead of here, e.g., “used to streamline editorial coordination and cross-department publishing workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear under Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp are similar; listing all four may feel padded unless each was used meaningfully.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools for your recent digital leadership work, but the item is too bare to signal level of use or strategic value. It should read as a focused platform list, not a repeat of your email experience already covered in NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform naming for consistency: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope/strength via parenthetical qualifiers, e.g. **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys (campaign automation)** • **Higher Logic (member communications/community)** • **Mailchimp (newsletter operations)**
- Keep it platform-only; let work experience carry outcomes like audience size, newsletter cadence, and channel leadership.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding phrases like “email newsletters,” “audience engagement,” or “campaigns” here in full-sentence form; those are already demonstrated in multiple NACo entries.
- If Dynamics 365 was only limited exposure, consider ordering by strongest/recentest platform instead of listing it first.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” In the technical section, it should read as a concise tools/methods list, not repeat broader capability language.

Suggested edit:
- Tighten and standardize: “GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Google Search Console • A/B testing”
- Replace vague terms like “Dashboarding” with the actual platforms already listed, or with “reporting” only if needed.
- Consider swapping “SEO” for “Google Search Console” or “SEO analysis” to make it more tool-/practice-specific.
- If space allows, order by strongest/recently evidenced tools from recent roles: “GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Power BI • Looker Studio • BigQuery …”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly repeats “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider trimming one of the two or making this section tools-only.
- “Dashboarding” overlaps with Looker Studio/Power BI and adds little on its own.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Emphasize foundational impact, team-building, and distinct early-career contributions rather than repeating web/video themes covered more strongly in 2018–2024 roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to stress “built from scratch” impact: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social media and multimedia.”
- Make contributions more concrete: add scope, frequency, or audience where possible (e.g., number of livestreams, cadence of weekly videos, size of site refresh, channels supported).
- Tighten phrasing and reduce soft verbs: replace “supporting the creation,” “contributed to,” and “high-impact” with direct action verbs like “helped launch,” “produced,” “streamlined,” and “supervised.”
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, streamline cross-channel publishing workflows, support a major website refresh, produce recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provide day-to-day supervision to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching or initially producing the series.
- Website/workflow language also appears in later NACo entries; frame this role as the foundation-building phase.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia/digital track, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo roles. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the policy/research support language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities, while contributing digital and multimedia content.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and strongest proof point: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Cut vague phrasing like “organizational programs and policy work” and “multimedia materials”; replace with more concrete terms such as “program teams,” “policy priorities,” “digital content,” or “audio production.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audience growth, internal stakeholders supported, or projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles; keep this entry focused on research/innovation support + first podcast launch.
- Avoid claiming broad digital leadership here, since stronger evidence appears in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” in Topline Skills. Use it to name specific tools only, not broader capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Creative & Audio/Video Tools**
